title: Routing Technologies and NAT

header.html: 2.1 Explain characteristics of routing technologies: static and dynamic routing (BGP, EIGRP, OSPF); route selection (administrative distance, prefix length, metric); address translation (NAT, PAT); first hop redundancy protocol (FHRP); virtual IP (VIP); subinterfaces
the official CompTIA Network+ N10-009 exam objectives, version 4.0

html:
1Static and dynamic routing

Type Meaning
Static routing An administrator enters each route manually; simple, predictable, no overhead; does not adapt to failures
Dynamic routing Routers exchange routes with a protocol and adapt to changes
Protocol Type Notes
OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) Link-state, interior Open standard, areas, metric = cost
EIGRP (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol) Advanced distance-vector, interior Cisco-origin, metric from bandwidth and delay
BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) Path-vector, exterior Routes between autonomous systems (the internet)

2Route selection

When several routes match a destination, the router chooses in this order:

Step Rule
1. Prefix length The most specific (longest) prefix wins, for example /26 beats /24
2. Administrative distance (AD) Lower AD = more trusted source
3. Metric Lower metric within the same protocol

Typical administrative distances: connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120 [Verify live].

Exam tip

. Longest prefix first, then administrative distance, then metric. A default route (0.0.0.0/0) is used only when nothing more specific matches.

3Address translation

Type Meaning
NAT (network address translation) Translates private to public addresses; static NAT one-to-one, dynamic NAT from a pool
PAT (port address translation, also NAT overload) Many private hosts share one public IP, distinguished by port numbers

4Redundancy and interfaces

Item Meaning
FHRP (first hop redundancy protocol, such as HSRP and VRRP) Two or more routers share a virtual gateway so hosts keep their default gateway if one fails
Virtual IP (VIP) The shared address hosts use as the default gateway; it moves to the surviving router
Subinterfaces Several logical interfaces on one physical router port, one per VLAN (router on a stick)
Exam tip

. "Clients must keep their gateway if one router fails" = FHRP with a virtual IP. "Route between VLANs with one router port" = subinterfaces (802.1Q trunk).

Exam tip

. OSPF is link-state and interior; BGP is path-vector and between organizations (autonomous systems).

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A router has routes to 10.1.0.0/16 and 10.1.5.0/24. A packet is sent to 10.1.5.20. Which route is used?

  • A10.1.0.0/16, because it covers more addresses
  • B10.1.5.0/24, because it has the longest prefix
  • CThe default route
  • DThe route with the highest metric
Show the answer

Answer: B. The most specific prefix wins.

S2A router learns the same prefix from OSPF (AD 110) and from a static route (AD 1). Which is used?

  • AThe OSPF route
  • BThe static route
  • CBoth equally
  • DNeither
Show the answer

Answer: B. Lower administrative distance wins.

S3Hundreds of private hosts must share one public IP address. Which technology fits?

  • AStatic NAT
  • BA first hop redundancy protocol
  • CPort address translation
  • DLink aggregation
Show the answer

Answer: C. PAT maps many private hosts to one public address using ports.

S4Which protocol exchanges routes between autonomous systems on the internet?

  • ABGP
  • BOSPF
  • CEIGRP
  • DRIP
Show the answer

Answer: A. BGP is the exterior path-vector protocol.

S5Hosts must keep a working default gateway if the primary router fails. What should be implemented?

  • AAn FHRP such as HSRP or VRRP with a virtual IP
  • BStatic NAT on the primary router
  • CA larger MTU on the uplink
  • DA second DHCP scope
Show the answer

Answer: A. FHRPs share a virtual gateway between routers.

S6A single router interface must route traffic for three VLANs. What configuration is used?

  • AThree separate DHCP relays
  • BPort mirroring on the switch
  • CThree NAT pools
  • DSubinterfaces on an 802.1Q trunk
Show the answer

Answer: D. Router on a stick uses a subinterface per VLAN.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is the first step of route selection?

Show the answer

The longest (most specific) prefix.

R2Which has the lower administrative distance, static or OSPF?

Show the answer

Static (1 versus 110).

R3What type of protocol is OSPF?

Show the answer

Link-state, interior.

R4What does PAT use to separate hosts?

Show the answer

Port numbers.

R5What does a VIP do in an FHRP?

Show the answer

Provides the shared default gateway address.

R6What is a subinterface?

Show the answer

A logical interface on a physical port, often one per VLAN.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Protocols static (manual), OSPF (link-state), EIGRP (advanced distance-vector), BGP (path-vector, between ASes)
Selection longest prefix, then lowest AD, then lowest metric
AD connected 0, static 1, eBGP 20, EIGRP 90, OSPF 110, RIP 120
NAT static and dynamic NAT; PAT shares one IP using ports
Redundancy FHRP (HSRP, VRRP) with a VIP; subinterfaces
